documents/BVTU-Constitution-and-Bylaws-2: Constitution CLAUSE 1 Name: The name of this society shall be Bulkley Valley Teachers' Union (“the Union”) and it shall be a Local of the British Columbia Teachers' Federation. CLAUSE 2 Objectives: The objectives of this society shall be: a) To represent its members and to regulate relations with their employer through: 1. collective bargaining of terms and conditions of employment, and 2. enforcement of the current collective agreement b) To raise the status and promote the welfare of the teaching profession in School District # 54 (Bulkley Valley). c) To promote the cause of education in the public schools of School District # 54 (Bulkley Valley). d) To carry on such activities as may from time to time be prescribed or approved by the British Columbia Teachers' Federation. CLAUSE 3 Boundaries The business of the society shall be carried on in School District # 54 (Bulkley Valley). 1 Bylaws BY-LAW # 1 - MEMBERSHIP a) Voting Membership: Voting membership in the Union shall be in accordance with the terms of the Constitution and By-laws of the British Columbia Teachers' Federation. Voting members shall be the only persons entitled to vote and hold office. Dues paying members, whether certified or uncertified, are voting members. Membership commences upon submission of a completed membership form to the Federation, or upon receipt by the Federation of applicable membership fees, whichever occurs first. Membership as a voting member ceases upon resignation, retirement, or termination of employment with a school district. b) Honorary Membership, Associate Lifetime, for the Past President, who retires and/or resigns from School District 54 to support the incoming president. This membership excludes voting and assumes no conflict of interest. BY-LAW # 2 - EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE a) The officers of this Union shall consist of a: President Vice-President Recording Secretary Treasurer Local Representative Bargaining Chair Grievance Chair District Joint Occupational Health and Safety Committee Representative French Language Representative Professional Development Committee Chair Political Action Contact Social Justice Contact Local Aboriginal Education Contact Past President (for one year only) TTOC Representative Other Committee Chair as established by the Union. In addition, one staff representative from each school will have a seat on the Executive Committee. 2 b) Dual Roles: A maximum of two officers on the Executive Committee can hold two roles. The President and the Treasurer MAY ONLY SIT in their roles. c) Duties of the Executive Committee: The Executive Committee shall, subject to the authority of General Meetings of the Union, govern the Union. d) Financial compensation for a local president to work from home in Houston: If an elected BVTU president lives in Houston, the BVTU will financially compensate for home office costs up to $1000.00 and transportation to/from Smithers up to $5000.00 [mileage at the CRA annual rate). Note: In the event the BVTU president lives in Houston, the Smithers BVTU office will be maintained for file storage and a meeting space. BY-LAW # 3 - DUTIES OF EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE OFFICERS a) The duties of officers and of the members of the Executive Committee shall be as defined in by the Simplified Robert’s Rules of Order (see BCTF Members’ Guide) when not in conflict with any clause of this Constitution. These rules shall also govern the procedure of all meetings of the Union. b) The newly elected Executive Committee shall, on July 1, assume the responsibilities for the affairs of the Union. c) The President shall be the presiding officer of the Union, and a member ex officio of all Committees and sub-Committees (appointed by the Executive Committee). They shall have general supervision of matters and affairs of the Union. d) The BVTU President will be compensated for up to 12 days of summer work in the form of lieu days taken during the school year; no more than two lieu days will be taken in a row. e) The Vice-President shall perform the duties of the President in their absence. f) Up to five release days are available to the Vice President to be used annually to build capacity and to prevent any interruptions in services provided to members in the event of the absence of the President. The five days can be exceeded with the approval of the BVTU EC in the case of an emergency involving the President. g) The Secretary shall keep accurate minutes of all meetings of the Executive and of all General Meetings. 3 h) The Treasurer shall: 1. Receive, disburse, and accurately account for all monies within the budget allocation. They shall disburse monies beyond this allocation only on the instructions of a majority at a General Meeting or on the instructions of a majority of an Executive Committee. 2. Deposit all monies received at a chartered bank and/or Credit Union to the credit of the Union and shall draw on these funds by cheque signed in accordance with a resolution of the Executive Committee. All cheques drawn on these funds shall be signed by the Treasurer and the President. 3. Prepare a budget for presentation to the Annual General Meeting of the Union. BY-LAW # 4 - ELECTIONS TO THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE a) All positions of the Executive Committee shall be filled by election at the Annual General Meeting except for Staff Reps (See By-law #2a), and Past President. Officers elected at the Annual General Meeting shall continue in office until June 30 of the following year. b) Nominations for positions of the Executive Committee can be sent in advance of the Annual General Meeting via email to lp54@bctf.ca. c) Nominations for positions of the Executive Committee can be received from the floor. Nominations from the floor: 1. Can be declined. 2. Must be seconded. 3. Will be voted on successively according to their order in By-Law #2a. d) Nominations for multiple positions are allowed, but as per By-Law #2b, only two seats on the Executive Committee can be dual role. d) Voting members only shall be eligible to vote and to hold office. A member shall be deemed elected by majority vote or by acclamation. e) Whenever a vacancy shall occur in the Executive Committee by death, resignation, or by removal from membership in the Union, the vacancy shall be filled by a General Meeting of the Union or through appointment by the Executive Committee until a General Meeting. f) Delegates to the Annual General Meeting or any Special General Meeting of the British Columbia Teachers' Federation shall be elected at a General Meeting of the Union. Voting procedures for delegates to the BCTF AGM shall be the same as the voting procedures followed at the AGM. Delegates are elected as representatives of the local and shall ensure that they seek feedback and input from the local and members on meeting business prior to attending. 4 BY-LAW #5 - EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE MEETINGS a) The Executive Committee shall meet at the call of the President or at the call of fifty per cent (50%) of its members. b) Executive Committee Meeting Quorum: Executive Committee meeting quorum shall be at least 50% of the seats (as per By-Law 2a). For funds to be disbursed at least 50% of the EC members must be present, one of whom must be the treasurer. If a member holds dual roles, quorum counts as one for each member. BY-LAW # 6 - GENERAL MEETINGS a) In addition to the Annual General Meeting there shall be at least two (2) regular General Meetings per year. b) At any General Meeting of the Union a quorum shall exist when there are ten per cent (10%) of the voting members present. If Quorum cannot be achieved: 1. The meeting will wait 15 minutes at which time those present will constitute quorum, and 2. The Agenda cannot be amended, and the powers of the meeting will be restricted as per the following: Quorum must be met to enable any General Meeting the power to vote on appointments, elections, ratifying agreements, or disbursement of funds above $100, unless otherwise required by BCTF policy and by-laws. BY-LAW # 7 - ANNUAL GENERAL MEETINGS a) Annual General Meetings of the Union shall be open only to voting members. b) The Annual General Meeting shall be held in April or May of each year for the purpose of: 1. receiving committee reports, 2. electing officers of the Union, 3. determining the budget for the following year, 4. disposing of such other business as may be brought before the Annual General Meeting. b) Notice of the Annual General Meeting shall be given to all members by the BVTU President via email not less than two weeks prior to the holding of the AGM. c) All meeting minutes will be circulated to members as soon as reasonably possible. 5 BY-LAW #8 SPECIAL GENERAL MEETINGS Special General Meetings shall be held at the call of the President, the Executive Committee, or at least twenty-five per cent (25%) of the voting members of the Union. Such Special General Meetings shall be held for any purpose properly to be considered by the membership and specifically for the purpose of ratification of a collective agreement or other business deemed necessary. Notice of Special General Meeting must be given to all members by the BVTU President via email not less than two weeks prior to the holding of the Special General Meeting. BY-LAW # 9 VOTING a) Voting at all meetings shall be limited to voting members. b) Voting at all meetings shall be by a show of hands except when a ballot is demanded by one-third of the members present. When necessary, voting during virtual meetings shall be either by a show of hands, or by anonymous polling (the results of each vote will be shared with the meeting). c) Secret balloting shall be used for elections, appointments, and ratifications. BY-LAW # 10 - COMMITTEES a) From time-to-time, committees may be formed by resolution of a General Meeting or of the Executive Committee. b) Each General Meeting will elect a chairperson to chair that meeting. c) The Executive Committee will elect a chairperson at each meeting to chair that meeting. BY-LAW # 11 - FEES a) The local fee shall be levied at the Annual General Meeting and shall be payable in accordance with the Constitution of the British Columbia Teachers' Federation. b) The amount of the local fee established at the Annual General Meeting shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and reported to the membership, including the applicable rate and the year in which it takes effect. BY-LAW #12: OPERATING RESERVE FUND a) The BVTU shall maintain an Operating Reserve Fund to ensure the financial stability and long-term sustainability of the Local. 6 b) Operating Reserve Fund shall be maintained at a minimum level equivalent to forty percent (40%) of the Local’s annual operating expenses, as determined by the most recently approved annual budget. c) The purpose of the Operating Reserve Fund is to provide financial security in the event of unforeseen expenses, revenue disruptions, legal costs, or other circumstances requiring unanticipated expenditures. d) The Executive Committee may approve by majority vote expenditures that temporarily reduce the Operating Reserve Fund below the prescribed minimum only where such expenditures are deemed emergent and/or necessary. e) Prior to considering approval, the Executive Committee shall receive and consider a written report outlining the rationale for the expenditure, the anticipated impact on the Operating Reserve Fund, and the plan and timeline for restoration to the minimum required level. f) The local shall report any approval under this section, including the rationale, amount, and restoration plan, to the next General Meeting and shall provide ongoing updates at subsequent General Meetings until the Operating Reserve Fund has been fully restored. BY-LAW # 13 - FINANCIAL REVIEW The accounts of the Union shall be reviewed by a General Accountant named by the Executive Committee. BY-LAW # 14 - INSPECTION OF BOOKS Any member of the Union shall, by giving ten days’ notice, have the right to inspect the books of account and records of the Union. BY-LAW # 15 - AMENDMENTS TO THE CONSTITUTION AND BY-LAWS The Constitution and By-laws may be amended by assenting vote of two-thirds or greater of the members present at the General Meeting if notice of such amendments shall have been circulated to the membership at least two weeks prior to the meeting. *Updated May 5, 2026 7

Awitzah! 4 ZONE 2 · PHIL BRIENESSE 5 Smithers / Glentanna / Driftwood · 3 seats to be elected Zone 2 On the ballot: Phil Brienesse, Frank Farrell (incumbent), Kristina Graham (incumbent), Diane Mackay, Casda Thomas NEW CANDIDATE · ZONE 2 Phil Brienesse Q1 Q1 Q2 + 2(a) Q3 Q4 Q5 Why are you running for trustee? I am running for school trustee because I have heard from parents, teachers and community user groups who feel disconnected from the Board and have had difficulty getting information, having their concerns heard, or navigating the district. I believe we can do better. I want to help build a culture of greater transparency, accountability and collaboration. In particular, I am concerned about the relationship between the Board, administration and teachers. These should be partners working toward the same goal: providing the best possible education for our students. I also believe we need to look creatively at how we support students in the early grades. K–3 is a critical period for establishing the foundation for lifelong learning, yet teachers are often trying to meet increasingly diverse needs without adequate classroom support. I want to explore how SD54 can better direct its resources toward early intervention and meaningful classroom supports. After seven years on Smithers Council, I understand both the responsibility of elected representatives and the importance of listening before making decisions. I want to bring that experience to the Board and help make SD54 more open, collaborative and responsive to the community it serves. Q2 + 2(a) Key education partners and community voices (answered together) Our key education partners include students and families, teachers and support staff, school administrators, PACs, the BVTU, Indigenous education partners, community organizations, user groups and the broader community. Each brings a different perspective, and all have a role to play in building a strong public education system. I absolutely agree that community voices should help guide the work of the district. BCSTA describes trustees as people who listen to their communities and guide the work of their school district, and I believe meaningful listening has to be an ongoing process, not something that happens only when a major decision is being made. As a trustee, I would make a point of regularly meeting with education partners and creating opportunities for people to raise concerns before decisions are made. Just as importantly, information needs to flow back to the community. People cannot provide meaningful input if they do not know what is being considered or where to find the relevant information. My goal would be to help make community engagement a normal part of how the Board operates rather than something that depends on individual trustees. If existing processes are not providing meaningful opportunities for engagement, I would work to improve them and, where necessary, seek out those conversations myself. ZONE 2 · PHIL BRIENESSE (CONTINUED) Q3 6 How would you raise a differing opinion? I think disagreement is an important part of good decision-making. If everyone around the table always agrees, we are probably not hearing enough different perspectives. If I disagreed with district staff or another trustee, I would raise my concerns respectfully, ask questions, listen carefully to the information being presented, and explain the reasons for my position. My experience on Smithers Council taught me that I can strongly disagree with someone while still respecting them and working with them toward a better solution. I also recognize that I may not have all the information. There have been times when I went into a Council meeting intending to vote one way and, through discussion and new information, changed my mind. That is not a weakness in decision-making; it is part of the reason we have a board. Ultimately, trustees are elected to participate in the collective governance of the district. I would stand up for my convictions and for concerns raised by the community, but once the Board has made a decision, I would respect that decision and work constructively with the other trustees to implement it. Q4 Would you vote for live streaming board meetings? Yes. I would support live-streaming Board meetings and making recordings available afterward. For many parents, teachers and community members, attending a Board meeting in person simply isn't practical. Livestreaming would make it much easier for people to understand how decisions are discussed and made, and recorded meetings would allow people to go back and review a particular discussion. Meeting minutes are important, but they generally record decisions rather than the full discussion that led to them. Public access to the actual conversation provides a much clearer picture of the questions being asked, the information being considered and the different perspectives around the table. I also think transparency needs to extend to meeting materials. Agenda packages, reports and the policies being considered should be easy for the public to find in one place. If the Board has access to information in preparing for a decision, the public should have access to the appropriate public portions of that same information. Making the process easier to follow would strengthen both public participation and accountability. Q5 Bonus: an educator who made a difference Many educators have made a difference in my life, but the one who comes to mind first is my high school English teacher. He taught me perhaps the most important lesson I took from school: how to think critically, form my own opinions, and support those opinions with evidence and facts. He was also the person who first got me interested in politics and community involvement. While I was in high school, the school board was considering cuts to Educational Assistant funding. Many students felt that this was the wrong place to make cuts. The Board held an open house, and my English teacher encouraged me to speak about how those cuts would affect students. I was one of only a few students who spoke that evening. I remember feeling that my voice actually mattered and that I could have an impact on decisions affecting my school. I want young people in SD54 to have that same sense that they can participate in their community and make a difference. I don’t see myself as an expert or someone who inherently has all the answers, but rather as a conduit between the community and the school district. I commit to being transparent about decision making, and available for dialogue with partners and community members. Q3 How would you raise a differing opinion? Having a group of trustees that can hold and discuss different opinions is good; it’s how we arrive at the best decisions possible. And fostering a culture of curiosity and respectful debate is healthy. When I served on Smithers town council, I regularly asked questions, voiced opinions and listened to what other councillors had to say. Sometimes what I said influenced our direction, other times something that another person said caused me to reconsider my position. I commit to sharing my perspective with the other trustees at the board table and to listening to their opinions with an open mind. This does not mean compromising my values. It means being open to different ways of arriving at the best possible outcomes. Q4 Would you vote for live streaming board meetings? Yes, I would be in favour of live streaming board meetings. This was the practice when I was on council and it was an excellent way for residents to engage at a level that worked for them. Few people have the time in their lives to attend board meetings but making them available online makes the meetings so much more accessible. Q5 Bonus: an educator who made a difference Mrs. Forrest, my grade seven homeroom and English teacher. There’s not one big thing that she did that sticks out for me, rather it was many small things that created a secure foundation for my first year in middle school. I don’t even think I realized or appreciated it at the time, but she is the teacher that consistently comes to mind when I think about my school years. She was strict, but also kind and calm. She asked us questions, respected our autonomy, and taught us about ‘real world things’ like personal wellbeing and compounding interest (this was not normal at the time!) If a student had menstrual cramps, they were free to leave the class and take care of themselves, and she would offer help discreetly, but without shame. She wasn’t everyone’s favourite teacher, it was quieter than that, she modeled stability, students respected her. She somehow created a safe space for all of us to just settle, be ourselves and let go of the constant pressure to fit in. The education of our young people is one of the most important responsibilities we have as a society. I want to see them properly equipped to understand their world and to take their places in it. Q2 Who are SD54’s key education partners? Students and their parents are at the centre of the education partnership. Teachers, of course, are the trusted partners with whom parents and students should have a positive relationship. Teachers, in turn, need a supportive administration team and that ultimately involves the board of trustees and other members of the community. Of course, many students are also instructed and influenced in their local churches / spiritual communities and in the clubs or teams to which they may belong. Q2(a) Should community voices guide the district, and how will you engage? Yes, I intend to be available to hear from the community and especially from parents. Nobody has a higher stake in the success and wellbeing of the children than their own parents. Q3 How would you raise a differing opinion? It’s likely that there will be differences of opinion. That’s why we elect boards or groups of representatives rather than just one person. We learn from each other and the goal is to find good solutions through the sharing of ideas and perspectives. It is my goal to communicate my thoughts and perspectives in a respectful manner. Q4 Would you vote for live streaming board meetings? I think so; I’d want to listen to the views of other board members first. I do believe in transparency so I don’t see any reason not to make the meetings accessible to the public. Q5 Bonus: an educator who made a difference I’ve been privileged to have a number of good educators / mentors in my life. I still do. My first educators, of course, were my Mom and Dad who both had a lasting and positive impact on my life. I also remember particularly my grade 2 teacher, my grade 6 teacher and my grade 7 teacher. My grade 6 teacher really boosted my confidence and encouraged me. There’s no doubt that a teacher can inspire, motivate and encourage a young person to learn and to achieve great things. I feel I would make a great trustee because of my background in education and my connections with the schools and community. I am friendly, organized, compassionate, and always strive to think outside the box for collaborative solutions. Also, this opportunity comes at a time when I am working part time and my kids are at the age where they are a bit more independent and I can dedicate the time that the role of school trustee deserves. Q2 + 2(a) Key education partners and community voices (answered together) Key education partners in the community are of course the staff and families of the students who attend our public schools. There are also various businesses and organizations with which the board could connect and collaborate, including local government, libraries, museums, community services, First Nations, sports clubs, special interest groups, farms, and emergency services to name a few. If elected as trustee, I would encourage community members to reach out to me with concerns and ideas to bring to the board. People who know me know that I love making connections! Q3 How would you raise a differing opinion? If I had the honour to have a seat at the board table, I would express my opinion even if it differed from the district staff’s opinions or another board member’s. Afterall, the purpose of the board having 7 members is so that no one person is making important decisions about the future of the school district and individual student needs. I realize that these conversations won’t always be comfortable, but I believe we can work collaboratively to reach a consensus that fits with the board values and has students’ best interests in mind. Once that decision is made, I would respect it knowing that my voice was heard along with 6 other voices and the communities we represent. Q4 Would you vote for live streaming board meetings? I do think it warrants a discussion on whether the live stream would be open to the whole world or whether there would be a way to allow only district residents to access the live stream. Q5 Bonus: an educator who made a difference I have so many positive memories of teachers, but I would have to say my high school French and Spanish teachers had a big impact in my life as my passion for languages and cultures started in their classes. They encouraged me to participate in a 2-month exchange to Quebec in grade 10 and a year-long exchange to ZONE 3 · KIM UNGER (CONTINUED) 14 Ecuador after graduating. I then went on to attend university in Japan and South Korea and also volunteered in Brazil, learning a few more languages along the way. Now, I share that passion with my adult EAL learners in my role as Language Instructor/ Assessor at Smithers Community Services Association. My 4 brothers and I all quit when we were in highschool. My parents didn't care. I quit when I was in grade 11 at PGSS in Prince George. Got married at 19 had 2 kids. NEW CANDIDATE · ZONE 4 Matt Williamson Q1 Q1 Q2 Q2(a) Q3 Q4 Q5 Why are you running for trustee? I am running as a candidate for school trustee for a few different reasons. Education is important to me, I believe that it is the foundation for building a successful life. I’d like to play a role in helping increase scholastic achievement in our district. I feel like the district and the board need to be more transparent and engaged with parents. I think that parents should have a proactive role in the education of their children in a way that compliments and encourages learning at school. I think that engaging with partners is very important, and I would commit to visiting schools and talking with staff and parents often. Q2(a) Should community voices guide the district, and how will you engage? I believe that the voice of the community should carry weight. If people are willing to have open and honest conversations about the education of their children, then that should be a priority and I would really like to see a lot of parental engagement with the board. I think that as trustees, we should not rely solely on things like studies from the provincial government, etc. British Columbia is a vast province with a very diverse population, so what works for a district on Vancouver Island or the Lower Mainland may not necessarily work for our small northern district and the people we serve. Our demographics are different and our logistics are more challenging. For example on logistics, in Vancouver it is only a matter of hopping ZONE 4 · MATT WILLIAMSON (CONTINUED) 18 on public transit for a Science World field trip during school hours, whereas in the north, we don’t have those transportation and destination options without considerable effort from staff and parent committees (not to mention the bussing issues we face here). Coincidentally, this could also have a beneficial environmental impact as well if more people watched from home. While we take these sorts of things for granted these days, back then it lit a spark that turned into a lifelong interest in computers and electronics. This in turn guided my choices in post secondary education and led me to amateur radio which was the basis of all the emergency communication volunteerism that I continue to pursue to this day!

documents/student-loan-forgiveness-appli: Employment and Social Development Canada Emploi et Développement social Canada Application for Canada Student Loan Forgiveness Important Your completed application form must be signed after the last day of your 12-month loan forgiveness period and submitted no later than 90 days after the last day of your 12-month loan forgiveness period. Applications received after the 90 days will be refused and you will have to apply again. Make sure you complete the entire application. If any information is missing, you might have to complete a new application and send it back to the National Student Loans Service Centre (NSLSC). You must send your application and all Employment Attestation forms together. If they are sent separately, your application will be rejected. About loan forgiveness The Government of Canada offers Canada Student Loan Forgiveness to eligible professionals who work in eligible communities. Loan forgiveness can only be applied to outstanding Canada Student Loan balances. Canada Student Loans that have been converted to a line of credit, private loan, or an Ontario Medical Resident Loan, are not eligible for loan forgiveness. Canada Student Loan Forgiveness applies only to the federal portion of a student loan. It does not apply to the provincial or territorial portion of a student loan. You can verify if your place of work is in an eligible community by using the Canada Student Loan Forgiveness Postal Code Lookup tool (http://tools.canlearn.ca/cslgs-scpse/cln-cln/lfnd-erpm/1-eng.do). Eligibility You can apply for loan forgiveness while you are in study. You can also apply if you are in repayment or in your six-month non-repayment period. To be eligible for Canada Student Loan Forgiveness you must: • • have a Canada Student Loan that is in good standing; and have practiced one of the following professions for a full year and provided in-person services for a minimum of 400 hours in an eligible community (the requirement to have worked a full year does not apply to residents in family medicine): • Registered Nurse • Licensed Practical Nurse • Nurse Practitioner • Registered Psychiatric Nurse • Registered Practical Nurse • Family Medicine Resident • Family Doctor • Dentist • Dentist Hygienist • Pharmacist • Midwife • Teacher (Kindergarten to Grade 12) • Social Worker • Physiotherapist • Psychologist • Early Childhood Educator • Personal Support Worker (see additional requirement below) Note: The 12 months of your loan forgiveness period are considered consecutive when you do not have a break in service of more than one month. See Section C – Break in service for the exceptions to this rule or if you were unable to work at least 400 hours. You cannot apply if you are restricted from receiving federal student financial assistance. However, you can apply if you are restricted only because you have received repayment assistance or if you are bankrupt but have kept your Canada Student Loan in good standing. Additional requirement for Personal Support Workers: In addition to the requirements listed above, Personal Support Workers must have worked as a personal support worker during the hours indicated for the period of time identified, meaning they provided one-on-one care and essential support to optimize and maintain their clients’ health, well-being, safety, comfort and autonomy. The services provided must be consistent with their clients’ healthcare needs as identified by a regulated healthcare professional or a community or provincial health organization. Licensing or Registration requirements You must have a valid license or registration from a province or territory and meet all professional requirements to practice one of the professions listed under the Eligibility section, with the following exceptions: • Family medicine residents are exempt from full license, but they must hold appropriate authorization from the province or territory. • Personal Support Workers are exempt from Licensing. • Physiotherapists working in Northwest Territories and Nunavut are exempt from Licensing. This exemption does not apply to other provinces or territories. • Early Childhood Educators working in New Brunswick, Northwest Territories, and Nunavut are exempt from Licensing. This exemption does not apply to other provinces or territories. ESDC SDE0094 (2025-10-FINAL) E Page 1 of 5 How much you could receive in Canada Student Loan Forgiveness As an Early Childhood Educator, Dental Hygienist or Personal Support Worker, you could receive up to $15,000 in Canada Student Loan Forgiveness over a maximum of 5 years, allocated as follows: • Year 1: $2,000 • Year 2: $2,500 • Year 3: $3,000 • Year 4: $3,500 • Year 5: $4,000 As a Nurse Practitioner, Registered Nurse, Registered/Licensed Practical Nurse, Midwife, Teacher, Social Worker or Physiotherapist, you could receive up to $30,000 in Canada Student Loan Forgiveness over a maximum of 5 years, allocated as follows: • Year 1: $4,000 • Year 2: $5,000 • Year 3: $6,000 • Year 4: $7,000 • Year 5: $8,000 As a Family Doctor and Family Medicine Resident, Dentist, Psychologist or Pharmacist, you could receive up to $60,000 in Canada Student Loan Forgiveness over a maximum of 5 years, allocated as follows: • Year 1: $8,000 • Year 2: $10,000 • Year 3: $12,000 • Year 4: $14,000 • Year 5: $16,000 In total, you can receive up to five periods of Canada Student Loan Forgiveness, even if you change from one eligible occupation to another. These periods do not need to be consecutive; however, they cannot overlap and your application must be submitted within 90 days after your loan forgiveness period end date. Eligible communities An eligible community is a population centre with a population of 30,000 or fewer, as defined by Statistics Canada and as determined by the most recent Census of Population, or a rural area, based on data published in the most recent census. Note: On a temporary basis, the previous definition of an eligible community, as follows, is also applicable for family doctor, family medicine residents, nurses, and nurse practitioners only (until 2026 Census of Population data is implemented): a municipality (as determined by Statistics Canada) that is located outside of: • • • census metropolitan areas; census agglomerations (geographic units) with an urban core population of 50 000 or more; and provincial capitals. Note: If you continue to work in an eligible occupation in a community for which you received the forgiveness benefit in the previous year, you remain eligible to receive the forgiveness benefit, even if it is no longer considered an eligible community. You can verify if your place of work is in an eligible rural or remote community by using the Canada Student Loan Forgiveness Postal Code Lookup tool (http://tools.canlearn.ca/cslgs-scpse/cln-cln/lfnd-erpm/1-eng.do). The name of your eligible community is required to complete your Employment Attestation(s) and must match the postal code exactly to be accepted. Loan forgiveness period To determine your loan forgiveness period, you select 12 consecutive months during which you were employed or in practice in an eligible community and you provided in person services for a minimum of 400 hours. Note: You must complete a full 12-month loan forgiveness period before you can apply for this benefit. The next loan forgiveness period you wish to apply for must begin after your previous 12-month loan forgiveness period has ended. Family medicine residents may apply as soon as they accumulate 400 hours of inperson service but may only apply once per 12-month period. If you worked in more than one eligible community during your loan forgiveness period to accumulate a minimum of 400 hours of in-person services, complete a separate Employment Attestation for each eligible community, listing your additional employment in chronological order. List your employment history during the loan forgiveness period, starting with your most current employment situation and working backwards. The number of months that you identify for each employment period on your Employment Attestation(s) must total 12 months to reflect a complete 12-month loan forgiveness period. Note: If you are a teacher, social worker, early childhood educator, or psychologist who works for a school, your loan forgiveness period is still 12 months, but your Employment Attestation(s) must total 10 consecutive months of employment within that 12-month loan forgiveness period. documents/ttoc-experience-credit.pdf: Understanding Article C.4 Teacher Teaching on Call Employment If you work as a Teacher Teaching on Call, you will earn experience credit under Article C.4 and LOU 11. This experience accumulates in your TTOC silo. TTOC Days worked If you also work in a contract, temporary or continuing, part time or full time, you will earn experience credit according to your local collective agreement provisions. This experience accumulates in your contract silo. 170 full days = 1 year 17 full days = 1 month Experience in your contract silo is governed by your local collective agreement (CA) provisions. You will find these provisions in the B section of your CA. ! NOVEMBER 15 | JUNE 30 Under LOU 11, you can move your TTOC experience credit into your Contract silo two times a year: November 15 and June 30. This is important because it will allow the two amounts of experience credit to be combined towards moving to the next step on the salary grid. Experience Credit is always moved from the TTOC silo to the Contract silo in one-month increments. If you request the transfer, all full months of experience will be moved to your contract silo. Fractions of experience less than 17 days will remain in your TTOC silo to be combined with future days. Before you decide about moving your TTOC experience, you should find out how much credit you have in each silo. It should be provided on your pay statements. If not, contact your District to request that information. Requests to move experience made by November 15 will be effective December 31 and request made by June 30 will be effective August 31. You must make the request using the agreed upon form available from your school district, prior to the deadline. Once the form is submitted, the decision to transfer your experience credit is final.
